finding.claim: prevIndex is tested for truthiness, so when the first slash is at index 0 (leading-slash input like "/foo") prevIndex becomes 0 and is treated as falsy. The final tokens update is skipped, leaving the last token value as '' and maxDepth under-counted.
finding.title: Falsy zero check skips last token update for leading slash

verifier.reason: At scan.js:382 prevIndex is set to the slash index i, so for "/foo" it becomes 0, and the guard at scan.js:390 tests prevIndex for truthiness, causing the last-token assignment and depth accounting at scan.js:391-393 to be skipped.

repro.expectedBehavior: scan with tokens returns the final path segment in the last token and counts its depth in maxDepth, including for a leading-slash pattern.
repro.rationale: Control 'foo/bar' has prevIndex=3 (truthy) so the final token update runs. Test '/foo' has its only slash at index 0, so prevIndex=0 is falsy and the update at scan.js:390 is skipped, leaving the last token '' and maxDepth at 1 instead of 'foo'/2.
